newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's BNDES denies CVRD conflict of interest.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's BNDES denies CVRD conflict of interest.

text.p: Brazil's National Development Bank, which is overseeing the sale of Cia Vale do Rio Doce, on Thursday denied conflict of interest allegations in connection with next week's planned auction of the state mining company.
In a statement, the bank said its vice president, Jose Pio Borges, was a member of the administration council for Aracruz Celulose, which is partly controlled by South Africa's Anglo American Corp.

The president of a Sao Paulo bankers union said Borges' membership on the Aracruz council and his position as director of Brazil's privatization drive represented a conflict of interest because Anglo American belongs to a consortium that is expected to bid for CVRD on Tuesday.

The bank denied Borges' involvement in Aracruz was not a conflict of interest because the BNDES owns a 12.5 percent stake in Aracruz and Borges was merely representing the bank on the Aracruz council, for which he receives no money or "advantages."
"There is no relation whatsoever between (Borges') representation of the BNDES on Aracruz's Administrative Council and his role as director of the national privatization program," the statement said.
The allegation is another potential obstacle that could block the goverment's plans to bring CVRD to the auction block. The sale also faces dozens of legal challenges.
